body: The Anchorage Community Development Authority filed a complaint on July 21, 2026 in state Superior Court against Hughes Family LLC and Anchorage Innovation District LLC, seeking a court-ordered sale of the former Nordstrom building at Sixth Avenue and D Street, the Anchorage Daily News reported on August 12. The three-story building has been vacant since 2019, when Nordstrom closed after 44 years there.

ACDA owns 80% of the building, four of its five lots, according to the Daily News. The fifth lot belongs to Hughes Family LLC, which is owned by four individuals, and which has an agreement with Anchorage Innovation District LLC to develop its share. Anchorage Innovation District is owned and managed by entities tied to developer Mark Pfeffer. The complaint says ACDA is at "an impasse" with the two companies over how to redevelop the property and argues that the building cannot be divided with a party wall or partition. It asks the court to order all five lots sold and the proceeds split proportionally.

In February 2026, Mayor Suzanne LaFrance's administration announced plans to convert the building into an "iconic development that would anchor downtown." At a July 17 Assembly committee presentation, ACDA director Mike Robbins said the project was more than a year from starting and that construction could begin next fall. Neither ACDA nor its attorney responded to the Daily News, and Hughes and Pfeffer Development did not respond to requests for comment. As of the article's publication, no further court action was scheduled. The Daily News later updated the article to clarify aspects of the Nordstrom and JCPenney garage projects.
